Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home

Negative Appraisals.value: The event happened because of the way I acted
The people responsible have faced no consequences
I feel ashamed of what happened to my body

vignette: Lena, a 28-year-old South Eastern Asian woman working as a tax consultant, sought help after experiencing severe psychological distress following her captivity. The traumatic event left an indelible mark on Lena's psyche, with the memory of being held captive haunting her every moment. Lena vividly recalls the day she was kidnapped while walking home from work. She had been targeted by a group that saw her as vulnerable due to her quiet demeanor and apparent lack of protection. The experience left her feeling stripped of control over her body and life, leading to intense self-blame. "If only I had been more cautious," Lena often thought, believing that the event was somehow her fault. The fear of being caught off guard has permeated every aspect of her daily life. Unexpected movements around her now trigger a visceral reaction as if she were still in danger. At work, when colleagues suddenly enter her office, Lena jumps out of her skin and feels a rush of adrenaline. This heightened startle response is compounded by her constant need to have her back against the wall wherever she goes. She feels safest only when she can see everything happening around her, which makes navigating her daily routine exhausting. Lena's apartment has become another battleground for her fears. Every creak and sound outside her door triggers a wave of anxiety as she listens intently for any sign that someone might be trying to enter. This intrusion monitoring keeps her on edge, constantly vigilant but never truly at ease. Her captors faced no consequences for their actions, adding to Lena's sense of injustice and despair. The lack of accountability has deepened her feelings of shame and self-blame, creating a cycle where the constant threat she perceives reinforces her negative beliefs about herself. "If they could get away with it," she thinks, "then maybe I did deserve what happened." This cognitive loop tightens as Lena's fears and self-doubt reinforce each other. The more she feels threatened by unexpected movements or sounds, the stronger her belief that she is to blame for the trauma becomes. Her occupation as a tax consultant has been significantly impacted; she avoids social gatherings with clients and colleagues due to her heightened vigilance and fear of being caught off guard. Lena's body shame is another pervasive issue. She feels humiliated by what happened to her, believing it tainted her in an irreversible way. The physical reminders of that time make her feel unworthy and less than human, further feeding into her negative self-image. The cumulative effect of these symptoms has left Lena isolated and desperate for relief. What finally brought her to seek help was a moment at work when she froze during a presentation due to the sudden appearance of a colleague in the room. This public display of her distress was a turning point, pushing her to realize that she needed professional support. Lena is most afraid of never truly feeling safe again and of being trapped by her own mind. She hopes for a future where she can regain control over her life and overcome these persistent fears and negative beliefs.
